curated.instructions: omr/instructions/42102-1-1.pdf (one book, 56 pages; the tractor is steps 1-54, pages 4-51, and page 52 shows its functions)

functions.does: The black 12 tooth gear on top of the cab steers the front wheels: its shaft runs down to a 16 tooth gear, which drives a second 16 tooth gear and then a third on the steering post between the front wheels; that post's arm swings the two steering knuckles.
functions.source: book: steps 1-7 (knuckles and steering gears), steps 10-12 (the gear train), step 53 (the shaft and gear on top), page 52 (curved arrow)

functions.does: Pushing the tractor along spins the two rake wheels behind it: the tan 20 tooth bevel gear on the rear axle drives a 12 tooth bevel gear on a shaft running back to the rake, where a 12 tooth gear turns a vertical gear between the two big rake gears, so both turn the same way.
functions.source: book: steps 37-39 (the shaft and its gears), steps 46-49 (the rake gears and the rear axle's bevel gear), page 52 (arrows round the rake)

functions.does: The rotary rake lifts up behind the tractor: the lime arm it hangs from swings up, and the rake rides up with it.
functions.source: book: page 52 inset (arrows on the black connector at the top of the arm and on the rake); steps 41-42 and 50-52 show how it hangs
functions.note: inferred: what pivots isn't clear from the book. The inset's top arrow is drawn on the black 3-long connector p116 42003 at the arm's top, as if it were a handle turning with the arm; the rake also hangs on a hinged bracket round its drive shaft (step 39), which may let it tip sideways

functions.does: The four wheels roll freely: each front wheel on its own short axle in its steering knuckle, the two rear wheels together on the 7-long rear axle that drives the rake.
